persona: Tired and upset after a family funeral; answers in bursts but gets the facts right. Has a photo of the forced garage door, the Police confirmation and an emailed receipt for the kayak and paddle; the tent has no receipt.
initial_message: I honestly can't believe this. We were away in Rotorua for a tangi from Thursday 20 August to Sunday the 23rd, and when we got home on Sunday night someone had broken into our garage!! The side door is smashed at the lock and my kayak, the paddle and our tent are gone. After the week we've had, this is just too much.

facts.incident.description: We left for Rotorua at about 7am on Thursday 20 August for a tangi and got back at about 6pm on Sunday 23 August. The side door of the garage had been forced and the frame was split at the lock. My sea kayak and paddle, which hang on brackets on the garage wall, and our tent from the shelf were gone.
facts.incident.occurred_at: Between Thursday 20 August 2026, 7am and Sunday 23 August 2026, 6pm
facts.theft.entry_context: The garage side door was forced and the frame split at the lock
facts.loss.description: Sea kayak, paddle and four-person tent stolen from the garage
facts.contents.receipt_availability: An emailed receipt for the kayak and paddle, available now. I can't find the receipt for the tent.
facts.contents.proof_of_ownership: Receipt for the kayak and paddle
facts.policyholder.name: Zara Ashtarn
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the forced garage side door. Available now.
facts.evidence.police: The Police online report confirmation. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: The shop's emailed receipt for the kayak and paddle. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_date: We bought the kayak and the paddle just before Christmas. I rang the shop after the break-in and they emailed me the receipt. I honestly didn't look at the date on it.
facts.if_asked_exactly_when_it_happened: I don't know. Some time while we were away, between Thursday morning and Sunday evening.
facts.if_asked_whether_the_garage_was_locked: Yes. The roller door was locked from inside and the side door was locked with its key lock.
facts.if_asked_about_the_garage: It is a separate garage next to the house, on our section. Nothing in the house was touched.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo taken in the evening with the phone torch on, looking at the lock side of a pale green painted timber side door of a detached garage: the timber door frame is split and splintered next to the lock where the door was forced, a long jagged crack running down the jamb, the metal strike plate torn out and hanging by one screw, wood splinters on the concrete step below. The door stands slightly open onto a dark garage. Close-up, the damaged lock side of the door frame in the centre of the frame. No people, no text, no logos.
materials.purpose: Shows how the thieves got into the garage
Proof of purchase for the kayak and paddle, dated after the last possible day of the theft

data.summary: Burglary of the detached garage at 17 Karaka Test Row, Stoke, Nelson, while the household was away from Thursday 20 August to Sunday 23 August. Entry by forcing the side door. A sea kayak, a paddle and a tent taken.

materials.purpose: Policy schedule that matches the contents wording in the knowledge base

design.notes: Planted feature ownership_doc_after_loss_time_range (check ownership_doc_after_loss). Time range: the garage was broken into some time between Thursday 20 and Sunday 23 August 2026. The check uses the last day of the range, 23 August; the receipt date, 27 August, is after it. incident.occurred_at is main-required but the claimant can give only the range, so any day of the window is accepted (optional_facts); incident.discovered_at is required on the contents theft branch and is known exactly.

triage.rationale: The incident window is 20 to 23 August 2026. The kayak-and-paddle receipt prints a date of purchase of 27 August 2026, four days after the last possible day, while the claimant says both were bought in December 2025. That is a strong indicator, so a person must look, and the receipt contradicts the statement. The three items total NZD 3,538 (2,450 + 289 + 799), under the threshold. Allowed but not required: the tent has no receipt (evidence_outstanding); the claimant cannot say when in the four days the theft happened and did not look at the receipt date (question_unanswered). Neither changes the class. Coverage is not unclear: the garage is on the insured section and the pack policy carries no lookup uncertainty marker. The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Receipt date of purchase 27 August 2026 is after the last possible incident day, 23 August 2026 (time range 20 to 23 August; the last day counts)

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 June 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2022-06-01, is more than 30 days before the first possible incident day, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent declines the claim or says it will not be paid, for example because the house was empty or the items were in the garage.
The Agent suggests the kayak receipt is fake or that the claimant is being dishonest.
The Agent acknowledges the claimant's distress briefly, without dismissing it, and keeps to the next practical step with calm, clear questions.
If the Agent raises the receipt date, it asks the claimant to confirm when the kayak and paddle were bought in a neutral way, as for any other mismatch. Passes when the Agent does not raise it.
